meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Bebo un vaso de agua fresca.
examples.trans: I drink a glass of cool water.

examples.text: Bebimos zumo de naranja en el desayuno.
examples.trans: We drank orange juice at breakfast.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Plural cajones.

examples.trans: The drawer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cajones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the drawers from the door.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Camino veinte minutos hasta el centro.
examples.trans: I walk twenty minutes to the city centre.
We walk slowly across the bridge.

meanings.note: Adjective from cerrar.

examples.trans: It is a closed piece.
Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Seen on shop doors opposite tirar (pull).

examples.text: Empuja la puerta de madera suavemente.
examples.trans: Push the wooden door gently.

examples.text: Empujamos la mesa hacia la sombra.
examples.trans: We pushed the table into the shade.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsula exclamation of approval.

examples.trans: It is a great piece.

examples.text: Genial. Dime todo lo que necesito saber.
examples.trans: Great. Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.
What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.
She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

meanings.note: Impersonal stem-changing verb (o -> ue: llueve).

examples.trans: Today it is raining heavily in Valencia.
Last night it rained until ten.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.
Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: De nuevo is an idiom meaning 'again'.

examples.trans: It is a new piece.

examples.text: ¡Ah, se abre! Gracias. Soy Clara, la nueva recepcionista.
examples.trans: Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am Clara, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Precede the verb alone (nunca llega tarde) or follow no.

examples.text: Nunca he visto ese cofre antes.
examples.trans: I have never seen that chest before.

examples.text: El tren de la mañana nunca llega tarde.
examples.trans: The morning train never arrives late.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.
The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for a computer.

examples.trans: The computer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ordenadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the computers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

perder.gloss: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)

meanings.en: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pierde).

examples.text: Date prisa o perdemos el tren.
examples.trans: Hurry up or we will miss the train.

examples.text: La tubería vieja perdía unas gotas.
examples.trans: The old pipe was leaking a few drops.

meanings.note: Metal lever handle on a door.

examples.trans: The door handle is here.

examples.text: Vemos los picaportes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the door handles from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

razón.gloss: reason; right (tener razón = to be right)

meanings.en: reason; right (tener razón = to be right)
meanings.note: Tienes razón = you are right; con razón = no wonder.

examples.trans: The reason is here.

examples.text: Vemos las razones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reasons from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for el/la recepcionista.

examples.trans: The receptionist is here.

examples.text: Vemos las recepcionistas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the receptionists from the door.

meanings.note: House rule or measuring ruler.

examples.trans: The rule is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reglas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rules from the door.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)
meanings.note: Irregular: sé, supe; sabe igual que = it tastes just like.

examples.trans: Do you know where the wrench is?

examples.text: Este bizcocho sabe a limón fresco.
examples.trans: This cake tastes of fresh lemon.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Uso gafas solo para leer letra pequeña.
examples.trans: I wear glasses only for reading fine print.
We use fresh lemons from the courtyard.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.
